synthesis.title: End-to-End CNN Steering vs. Mid-Level RNN Trajectory Prediction Approaches
synthesis.body: There is a contradiction between the approach of using a CNN that learns the entire processing pipeline to steer an automobile (claim e66d15a0-9347-5814-b053-1ff1dea8058d) and the approach of using ChauffeurNet, an RNN that takes mid-level input and outputs driving trajectories for control (claim cc49c2d4-b50d-5322-8525-304268249b24). The disagreement lies in the level of abstraction and input representation used: the CNN approach operates end-to-end from raw sensor data to control commands, while the RNN approach relies on mid-level representations and predicts trajectories rather than direct control commands. This reflects differing methodologies in autonomous driving system design, with implications for training, interpretability, and robustness.
